title: eventmodeling canonical envelope
description: Mermaid 11.15.0+ eventmodeling: a timeline of Time Frames (UI/processor, command, event, read model) with inferred swimlanes, optional data, and reset points (see reference/syntax/eventmodeling.md). This target always emits the DSL's compact token form (tf/rf, ui/pcr/cmd/rmo/evt) for determinism; the relaxed spelling is a pure input-syntax alternative Mermaid also accepts and this IR does not need to reproduce.

accessibility.description: Confirmed by render (mermaid-cli 11.16.1): accTitle/accDescr produce an error SVG for eventmodeling today, unlike most other diagram types, so this target intentionally does not accept accessibility content.

number.description: Unique Time Frame reference number; order in the array is display order, not numeric order.

reset.description: true emits a Reset Frame (rf), breaking automatic inference from the prior frame; false emits a normal Time Frame (tf).

type.description: ui=UI, pcr=Processor (both UI/Automation swimlane); cmd=Command, rmo=Read Model (Command/Read Model swimlane); evt=Event (Events swimlane).

entity.description: Entity Identifier, optionally namespaced as 'Namespace.Entity' — each Namespace+type pair forms its own swimlane.

data.description: Inline data for this Time Frame, e.g. `{ description: string }`. Mutually exclusive with dataRef.

dataType.description: Optional backtick-prefixed type tag on inline `data`, e.g. `json`{ ... }.

dataRef.description: References content.dataBlocks[].id via `[[identifier]]` instead of inline data. Mutually exclusive with data.

relations.description: Explicit `->>` chain of other timeframes' `number`s this frame relates to (e.g. a read model built from multiple events).

id.description: Referenced from a Time Frame's dataRef via [[id]]; suffix repeated entities to keep ids unique.

value.description: A JSON number always renders bare (e.g. 20.4). A JSON string renders single-quoted (e.g. 'john') unless raw is true.

raw.description: true emits a string value unquoted — used for type declarations like `description: string` rather than literal values.
